Messages.Author: Nikolaj "Lord of the Betrayers" Wendt
Messages.Body:
I tried to compile the issues people currently have with two player
format and order them a bit. They are listed below each with A, B, C
etc.
After that I took some of the suggested formats and tried to come up
with some others, plus I tried to note down which (if any) of the
issues I felt this solution would improve. If included in paranthesis
it is because they might only partially help with that particular
issue.

Please add more possible solution or suggestions if you have them, or
comment on some of the ones below.

ISSUES:

A- Some stable cards are useless.
B- Some cards with "X players" in the effect become too weak.
C- Cards that a passed on to predator or prey can break the game.
D- Certain deck types (especially weenie decks) are too strong, as
there are no other players to help you against them.
E- Having the Edge is too strong, and it becomes too easy to hold on
to it.
F- Lack of interaction based on the two deck types can make the game
boring.
G- Rock-Paper-Scissor can screw you over more so than in a normal
game.
H- Combat decks, or decks that target minions are too strong, as they
only have to focus on "half" as many minions as usually.
I - Lack of player-player interaction makes the game too simple and
boring compared to a 5 player game.

POSSIBLE SOLUTIONS

1:
• You must burn the edge to gain a pool at your untap.
• Any bleed redirection costs at least 1 blood for minion cards and 1
pool for master cards or effects and makes the bleed action fail.
• Any X referring to the number of players is =3
• Start with 40 pool and 4 transfers every turn
Help with A, B, (D), E

2:
In addition to option 1, add the following:
• You can only take ONE action targeting your opponent or cards
controlled by him per turn.
• You can only block ONE of your opponents actions per turn.
Helps with A, B, D, E, H,

3:
• Add 2 imaginary players with only pool (15, 20 or 30)
Helps with B, C, (E)

4:
• In addition to option 2 the imaginary players each receive two 1 cap
vampire in their untap phase. One vampire will try to bleed for 1 with
no stealth. If in combat he plays no cards and attempts to strike for
1. The other vampire will remain untapped and attempt to block any
action (normal prey/predator order) and if in combat will play no
cards.
• At the beginning of the untap phase the imaginary player also
removes the vampires from the previous turn from the game.
Helps with A, B, C, (D), E, (I)

I was thinking about writing some of these out, print them on paper
with a note/comment field and bringing them to the NAC. Maybe try and
get some people involved in trying the different formats out over the
week and then compile it all at the end of the week.

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Nikolaj "Lord of the Betrayers" Wendt wrote:
> POSSIBLE SOLUTIONS
>
> 1:
> ï¿½ You must burn the edge to gain a pool at your untap.

I don't think holding the Edge is problematic. Blocking decks themselves a
problematic, but Edge-holding is only a miniscule part of that.

That said, if you use this rule, you should errata the cards that allow burning
the Edge during your untap for some other effect to also gain the standard Edge
pool, then.

Sabbat Threat
Deploy the Hand
Hand Intervention
Lucinde, Alastor
burning 419 Operation
Alonzo Guillen
Extortion
Mapatano Utando
Tragic Love Affair

Arguably Sarrasine and Victoria as well (e.g., burn the Edge during your untap
phase to gain 1 pool and gain an MPA in your next master phase).

> ï¿½ Any bleed redirection costs at least 1 blood for minion cards and 1

> pool for master cards or effects and makes the bleed action fail.

This rule would certainly make Edge-holding easier. If Edge-holding is a
problem, you shouldn't use this rule.

Better: "Any effect that would change the target of the bleed instead reduces
the bleed amount by 1"

> ï¿½ Any X referring to the number of players is =3

Affects three cards (plus one banned card):
Turns ConAg into a weaker KRC. May as well play KRC.
Makes Parity Shift stronger, which isn't needed.
Turns Slave Auction into a unique STI. May as well use STI.

So, in all, not effective at addressing B except in making Parity Shift
stronger, and Parity Shift is strong enough in 2p as printed.

> ï¿½ Start with 40 pool and 4 transfers every turn

? Which "problem" is this addressing?
In any event, if you want more pool, fine. If you want faster influence, you
should still use the ramp: first player gets 2 transfers on first turn. Every
player gets 4 transfers on all other turns.

> 2:
> In addition to option 1, add the following:

> ï¿½ You can only take ONE action targeting your opponent or cards

> controlled by him per turn.

> ï¿½ You can only block ONE of your opponents actions per turn.

> Helps with A, B, D, E, H,

? How does that help with A?
B?

This rule just turns the game into a fatties-only game (esp. if combined with
the 40pool start). Which is fine if that's what you want, but it seems unnecessary.

You could implement a borrow-transfer system to help address D without going to
the extreme above:
During your influence phase, gain 6 transfers (3 for the first player on the
first turn).
Spend transfers as normal. Unused transfers are kept (use counters to track them).
Attempting an action costs a transfer.
Successfully blocking costs a transfer. (Or 2 if the acting minion is an older
vampire, bwahaha).

If banking them becomes a problem, add
At the start of your influence phase, burn all unused transfer counters you have
before gaining your 6 new ones.

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:

> I like that idea. Should probably be non-mandatory actions, and maybe
> only succesful actions instead of attempts.

It should be attempts, unless you also don't count successful blocks.

(You either get to peel off a block counter from your opponent or you get a
successful action. Either way, it's worth a counter of your own. Just like the
rules don't tap you only for successful actions: you tap whether your action is
successful or not).
